questions.prompt: Which motor family is the natural first choice for holding a camera steady at near-zero speed, driven directly with no gearbox?
options: A propeller outrunner with an ESC.
A high-resistance gimbal BLDC motor with a FOC driver and encoder.
A brushed gearmotor with a 160:1 gearbox.
A hobby servo with 20 kg-cm on the label.
questions.explanation: A gimbal motor has a high winding resistance (order 10 ohm), so the stall current at a few volts is small and the heat is manageable; a propeller motor of about 0.07 ohm would draw over 100 A at 11 V.

questions.prompt: A datasheet lists 30 kg-cm of stall torque. Give it in N m (1 kg-cm = 0.0980665 N m). Precision 0.005.
A joint needs 0.6 N m continuously and the motor's stall torque is 2.4 N m. What fraction of the stall torque is the working torque (as a fraction, not a percent)?
questions.explanation: 0.6 / 2.4 = 0.25, about the quarter-to-a-third guideline of HW05.

questions.prompt: A motor has a no-load speed of 120 rpm and a stall torque of 3 N m at its rated voltage. Using the two-point line, give its speed at a 0.75 N m load, in rpm. Precision 0.5.
What does a coreless (ironless) brushed motor remove, and what is the main consequence?
options: The magnets; it becomes a stepper.
The brushes; it needs no driver.
The iron core; it has no cogging and a light, fast rotor.
The gearbox; it turns at the load speed.
questions.explanation: No iron core means no iron teeth, so no cogging, much lower rotor inertia and low winding inductance (maxon academy, DC motor, p. 6 to 7).

questions.prompt: A rotor of 2e-6 kg m^2 sits behind a 50:1 gearbox. Give the reflected inertia at the output in kg m^2. Precision 0.0001.
A vertical axis must not fall when the power is cut. Which transmission choice can do that without a brake, in principle?
options: A ball screw (about 90 percent forward, 80 percent backdrive efficiency).
A lead screw whose lead angle is smaller than the friction angle.
A harmonic drive in a 100:1 ratio.
questions.explanation: A screw (or worm) whose lead angle is below the friction angle is self-locking; ball screws and low-ratio gears backdrive, and even self-locking pairs come with no guarantee (Boston Gear, Roton).

questions.prompt: Pick a motor family and a transmission for (a) a quadruped leg joint and (b) the vertical axis of a small pick-and-place machine, and say why they differ.
rubric: Leg: a large-gap BLDC with a low-ratio planetary (quasi-direct drive) and FOC, chosen for backdrivability and impact tolerance.
Vertical axis: a screw or belt axis with a stepper or servo, with a self-locking screw or a brake so the load holds when power is lost.
States the contrast: a joint that must react to contact is backdrivable, an axis that must hold a load is not.
questions.explanation: Rubric-guided: compare your answer with each rubric point; this question is not automatically graded.
